body.statement: Under ordinary nonparametric ADMG semantics, for every realization \(G_S\), ordinary \(\operatorname{ID}(G_S,P_x(y))\) fails if and only if there are nonempty vertex sets \(A\subseteq F_0\subsetneq F_1\subseteq V\) forming a hedge for the original query: each \(F_i\) is bidirected connected and admits a directed subgraph in which every vertex reaches \(A\), \(F_0\cap X=\varnothing\), \(F_1\cap X\ne\varnothing\), and every vertex of \(A\) reaches \(Y\) by a directed path in \(G_S[V\setminus X]\).

source.locator: Definition of a hedge on pages 6--7 and Proposition 1(1) on page 7
source.verbatim_statement: An \(\vec{R}\)-rooted C-forest is a bidirected connected set of vertices \(\vec{F}\) in \({\cal G}\) such that \(\vec{R}\subseteq\vec{F}\), and there exists a subgraph \({\cal G}^{*}_{\vec{F}}\) of \({\cal G}\) containing only vertices in \(\vec{F}\) and a subset of edges among \(\vec{F}\) such that \(\vec{F}\subseteq\operatorname{an}_{{\cal G}^{*}_{\vec{F}}}(\vec{R})\) (every element in \(\vec{F}\) has a directed path to an element in \(\vec{R}\) in this subgraph). A hedge for \(p(\vec{Y}\mid\operatorname{do}(\vec{a}))\) in \({\cal G}(\vec{V})\) is a pair of \(\vec{R}\)-rooted C-forests \(\vec{F},\vec{F}^{\prime}\) such that \(\vec{F}\subset\vec{F}^{\prime}\), \(\vec{F}\cap\vec{A}=\emptyset\), \(\vec{A}\cap\vec{F}^{\prime}\setminus\vec{F}\neq\emptyset\), and \(\vec{R}\) is an ancestor of \(\vec{Y}\) via directed paths that do not intersect \(\vec{A}\). Given \(p(\vec{Y}\mid\operatorname{do}(\vec{a}))\) and \({\cal G}(\vec{V})\) as inputs, the ID algorithm fails if and only if any one of the following conditions hold: There exists a hedge for \(p(\vec{Y}\mid\operatorname{do}(\vec{a}))\) in \({\cal G}(\vec{V})\).

attestation.note: Literal primary-source transcription from arXiv:2307.03750v1 HTML, hedge definition and Proposition 1(1), accessed 2026-09-13.

body.justification: This is the published original-query failure criterion used to convert graphical ID failure into a finite hedge witness.
body.gap: The result is imported at theorem granularity; all edge-labelled sparsification is derived in this note.
body.consumer: It supports failure monotonicity, sparse cores, and the width-two bow characterization.
